reply_text:
I'd hold the merge: there's one blocking bug. I didn't change any code. All the tests pass, but they don't catch the problem.

**Blocking: `canEdit` checks the wrong permission (src/guard.js)**
```js
return share.mask & WRITE === WRITE && !share.locked;
```
JavaScript checks `===` before `&`, so this runs as `mask & (WRITE === WRITE)`, which is `mask & true`, which is `mask & 1`. That's the **READ** bit, not WRITE. I tried it on your branch:
- A view-only share (`READ`) gets `canEdit` → **true**, so anyone with a viewer link can edit.
- A share with COMMENT and WRITE but no READ gets `canEdit` → **0** (counts as false).

The editor test passes only because editors also have READ. Fix it with `hasRight(share.mask, WRITE)`, the same way `canComment` does. Also add a test that checks a viewer can't edit.

**Minor issues**
- **`transferOwnership` doesn't check anything.** It never confirms that `fromUser` is the current `doc.owner`. If `fromUser` has no share, it quietly adds one with no rights (`undefined & ~ADMIN` → `0`). Whoever calls it has to do the authorisation check, so it's worth saying that or checking it inside the function.
- **`toggleRight` with more than one right at once.** It's fine for one switch, as the README describes. But if it's ever passed several rights together, it flips each one separately instead of turning them all on or all off. Also, nothing stops someone switching off READ while COMMENT or WRITE are still on. With the fix above, that leaves a share that can edit but can't view.
- **Missing tests.** Nothing tests switching a right off, a viewer trying to comment or edit, or what happens to the previous owner's other rights after a transfer.

Everything else looks good: `canComment`, the locking rules, the ownership masks, the README, the changelog and the 3.2.0 version bump.
